summary: Remove the task-specific heuristic about prioritizing positive findings over negative consensus from AGENT_SYSTEM to eliminate leakage/grader-gaming.

edits.hypothesis: Removing the hardcoded rule that biases the agent toward specific positive findings when tools disagree eliminates the task-specific leakage identified by the reviewer, restoring a neutral stance on tool conflicts while retaining the general instruction to re-examine pixels.
edits.why_not_lower_lever: The objection is strictly about the presence of a specific decision heuristic in the prompt that mirrors the ground-truth distribution of the evolve set; removing this text is the only way to satisfy the constitution's prohibition on hard-coded answer biases.
edits.trigger_condition: Always active for M5 arm agents using the AGENT_SYSTEM prompt.
edits.retroactive_check: (corrective) In q000009 and q000002, the agent will no longer receive an explicit instruction to override negative consensus with positive findings, which removes the leaked bias. (preservative) This does not disrupt successful habits where tools agree or where direct visual reasoning suffices. (transfer) Generalizes by removing domain-specific conflict resolution logic, making the harness more robust to different noise distributions.
edits.regression_risk: The agent may revert to uncritically accepting negative consensus in cases where a subtle positive finding was present, potentially lowering accuracy on those specific types of tasks, but this is required to comply with the no-leakage constraint.
edits.mechanism: Removing the hardcoded rule that biases the agent toward specific positive findings when tools disagree eliminates the task-specific leakage identified by the reviewer, restoring a neutral stance on tool conflicts while retaining the general instruction to re-examine pixels.
